title: Motivation
examples: What is the difference between Maslow's and Herzberg's ideas?
Can you give an example of Taylor's Scientific Management?
Which theory explains why people work hard even if they are paid well?

explain.say: Today we are learning about what motivates people to work hard.
Maslow's theory suggests we have needs in a pyramid shape.
Herzberg said some needs cause satisfaction, and some cause dissatisfaction.
Taylor focused on efficiency using scientific methods in the workplace.
For example, if a worker feels respected, Maslow says they feel good.
In real life, a company giving awards for good work uses Herzberg's ideas.

faq.q: Are these theories always correct for every job?
faq.a: No, motivation is complex and different jobs require different things. For instance, a creative job needs different motivators than a routine job.

faq.q: Does money solve all motivation problems?
faq.a: No, while money is important, theories show that things like recognition and job interest are also crucial for long-term motivation. Money addresses basic needs, but not higher ones.
asks: What is more important than pay?

faq.q: What is the main difference between Maslow and Herzberg?
faq.a: Maslow suggests a ladder of needs you must climb up. Herzberg separates needs into two groups: those that motivate and those that just stop you from being unhappy.
asks: How are Maslow and Herzberg different?
Which theory talks about two types of needs?

faq.q: How is Taylor's work different from modern management?
faq.a: Taylor focused heavily on breaking down every task into the simplest, most efficient steps. Modern management allows for more worker input and creativity.
asks: Is Taylor's way of working still used?
What is the flaw in Taylor's system?

faq.q: If I get a promotion, which theory explains my feeling?
faq.a: A promotion usually satisfies the esteem needs according to Maslow. It also provides recognition, which Herzberg calls a motivator.
asks: When I get a raise, what theory applies?

facts: Maslow's hierarchy suggests that lower-level needs must be met first.
Herzberg identified 'motivators' as factors that genuinely increase job satisfaction.
Taylorism emphasized time and motion studies to improve efficiency.
A salary increase addresses a basic need, but might not be enough to keep someone highly motivated.

quiz.say: A worker complains that the office chairs are uncomfortable and the air conditioning is poor.
quiz.why: These physical conditions relate to 'hygiene factors' which, if poor, cause dissatisfaction but do not motivate on their own.

wrong.0: This mixes the psychological needs of Maslow with the mechanical focus of Taylor.
wrong.2: Maslow would place physical comfort under safety, but Herzberg's model specifically separates these maintenance issues.
wrong.3: Taylor is concerned with the process of work, not the physical comfort of the environment.

quiz.say: A manager redesigns a product assembly line to reduce wasted movement.
quiz.why: This focus on optimizing every physical movement is the core idea of Scientific Management.

wrong.0: Herzberg is more interested in the job content and recognition than the physical movement paths.
wrong.1: These theories are too focused on internal needs to address pure mechanical efficiency.
wrong.3: Maslow deals with the worker's internal psychological needs, not the physical layout of the work.
